path: cvpr2026/Text-Printed Bridging the -Text Modality Gap for Text-centric Training.pdf
title: Text-Printed Bridging the -Text Modality Gap for Text-centric Training
one_line: 简单文本渲染增强LVLM文本理解，但依赖OCR能力且场景有限
innovations: Text-Printed Image (TPI) rendering text onto canvas
Preserving text semantics while bridging modality gap
Low-cost data augmentation strategy for LVLMs
method_framework: TPI renders text descriptions onto plain white canvas, processed by vision encoder while preserving semantics, bridging image-text modality gap without architectural modifications.
experiment_framework: Evaluated on 4 LVLMs across 7 benchmarks (ScienceQA, OK-VQA, VizWiz, ChartQA, InfoVQA, DocVQA, DriveLM), comparing with Text-only, Text-to-Image, and GT-Image baselines.
takeaways: Simple text rendering can effectively bridge image-text modality gap
TPI preserves text semantics better than text-to-image models
OCR capability correlates with TPI effectiveness
weaknesses: Effectiveness depends on visual encoder's text recognition capability
Limited evaluation on specialized medical imaging domains
Potential limitations with complex visual scenes beyond text
relevance_reason: 文本渲染增强LVLM，但未触及可靠性主线或落地域
